Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress Peter Obi, has promised to establish 10,000 primary healthcare centres and build 40,000 primary school blocks across the country if elected president in 2027. Obi said the proposed projects would improve access to healthcare and education, particularly at the grassroots. He made the promises on Friday during an NDC town hall meeting and homecoming event at the Main Bowl of the Archbishop C.J. Patterson Building, All Saints Cathedral, Onitsha, Anambra State. The former Anambra State governor said his administration would ensure that every ward in the country had a functional primary healthcare facility. “So, I’ll show you, we will ensure that there’s a functional primary care in every ward in Nigeria. We have 8,809 wards, but we have promised Nigeria that we’ll do 10,000 primary care. That’s what we are going to do,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources Obi also pledged to address the country’s out-of-school children crisis through the construction of 40,000 primary school blocks. He said the impact of the intervention would begin to be felt from the beginning of his administration. “What goes on, I have said, is that we have 18 million out-of-school children. From day one, people will see the reduction because we plan to do 40,000 primary school blocks. And we will do that,” he said. We will invest in education. We will invest in health. “We will invest in building that society that you’ll be proud of. That society that will care. No longer will a Nigerian want to go to Lagos and be scared about his safety,” he added. Obi’s appearance in Onitsha formed part of his campaign engagements ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The event, described as a homecoming for the former governor, followed a roadshow through parts of the commercial city and a visit to his alma mater, Christ the King College, Onitsha. Obi governed Anambra State between 2006 and 2014 and was the Labour Party’s presidential candidate in the 2023 general election. He is now seeking the presidency on the platform of the NDC, with former Kano State Governor Rabiu Kwankwaso as his running mate.
